Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second innings. Anamul Haque and Soumya Sarkar stride out to open for Bangladesh. It will be Adam Milne to start the proceedings with the ball. Here we go!
...THE RUN CHASE...

Bangladesh bowlers started well with the ball. Shoriful Islam was the pick of the bowlers with 2 for 28 in his spell while Hasan Mahmud was economical. The rest of the bowlers had an off day and were taken to the cleaners. Right then, the revised target for Bangladesh as per the DLS method is 245 in 30 overs. Can they chase this and get an early lead in the series? We shall find out. The second inning is coming your way shortly.

A fine finish from Will Young takes New Zealand to an excellent score of 239 in this rain-curtailed game. Batting first, New Zealand were two down inside the first over as both Ravindra and Nicholls were dismissed for ducks. Young and Latham did the rebuild with a 171-run stand and got the hosts in a commanding position. New Zealand were going steadily before the third rain break but once the game was reduced to 30 overs per side, the Kiwi skipper went berserk and scored runs all around the park. Latham departed on 92 while Chapman played a quick cameo of 20. The star of the batting innings was Will Young who batted sensibly early on and took on the bowling in the final few overs. New Zealand will be confident of defending this with the bowling attack they have in store.

TOSS - Bangladesh have won the toss and elected to field first.

Bangladesh, on the other hand, have named Najmul Hossain Shanto as their all-format leader and he is coming to the New Zealand shores with a pretty young and exciting squad. Litton Das will play a key role with the bat along with the skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto, Mushfiqur Rahim, and Towhid Hridoy. Mustafizur Rahman, Shoriful Islam and Hasan Mahmud will share the responsibility with the ball. Mehidy Hasan has been in brilliant form in the past year or so and will again need to come good with the bat and ball in the absence of Shakib Al Hasan. There are plenty of exciting names on both sides and this series promises to be a close affair. Who will draw first blood and take an early lead in the series? Let’s find out. Toss and team news in a bit. Stay tuned!

New Zealand have named a fairly new side for this series and have rested their regular players. Tom Latham will lead the unit which has the star of Cricket World Cup, Rachin Ravindra, and a couple of other members such as Mark Chapman, Will Young, and Ish Sodhi. The Kiwis have brought in some fresh faces in Josh Clarkson, William O'Rourke, and Ben Sears. New Zealand will be hoping that the new members grab their opportunity as and when it comes as they build up to the next cycle.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the 1st ODI in the Bangladesh tour of New Zealand. The hosts, New Zealand are taking on the visiting Bangladesh side in the first of the 3-match series at the University Oval at Dunedin.
... MATCHDAY ...

After a riveting Test series that had one of the best finishes to a Test match we have seen in recent times, New Zealand and Bangladesh meet again but this time it will be the white-ball format with 3 T20Is and 3 ODIs lined up. The Test series took place in Bangladesh but the caravan has moved to New Zealand for this white-ball series and the 1st ODI will be played in Dunedin. Both sides have tested a few players with the Kiwis notably resting big names like Kane Williamson, Devon Conway, Mitchell Santner, Trent Boult, Tim Southee and Daryl Mitchell for this series. Tom Latham will once again lead the side but they do have some young exciting talent to watch out for in the form of Finn Allen and Rachin Ravindra. Bangladesh also continue to be without Shakib Al Hasan and will be led by Najmul Hossain Shanto who seems to be the new permanent captain. The visitors on the other hand do have a pretty solid team with a good mixture of youth and experience. Litton Das will be the man to keep an eye on at the top of the order whereas Soumya Sarkar makes a return to the side. Mushfiqur Rahim continues to provide solidity to that middle order and the heavy lifting with the ball will be done by Shoriful Islam and Mustafizur Rahman in the absence of Taskin Ahmed. Can Bangladesh take advantage of a slightly weakened Kiwi line-up and start with a win? Or will home conditions make the difference for New Zealand? We shall find out.
